title: Indefinite 6: некого / нечего (No One / Nothing to ...)
description: The 'there is no one / nothing / nowhere / no time to do X' construction. Stress shifts to не- (нЕкого, not никогО), there is NO second не, the logical subject stands in the dative, and the verb is an infinitive: Мне нечего делать.
descriptionRussian: Конструкция «не́кого / не́чего / не́где / не́когда что-то делать». Ударение переходит на не- (не́кого, а не никого́), второго не нет, логическое подлежащее стоит в дательном падеже, глагол — в инфинитиве: Мне нечего делать.
intro: A family that looks like the negatives from lesson 4 and behaves in almost the opposite way. There is only one negation, not two. The person is in the dative rather than the nominative. The verb is an infinitive. And the stress sits on the prefix, which is the audible clue that tells the two families apart in speech.
rules: The не- family (некого, нечего, негде, некуда, некогда, незачем) means 'there is no one / nothing / nowhere / no time / no reason to do X.'
Stress is on the prefix не-: нЕкого, нЕчего, нЕгде, нЕкуда, нЕкогда. Compare the plain negative никогО (stress on the end). The flipped stress is the audible signal of this construction.
There is NO second не on the verb. This is the opposite of the lesson-4 negatives: Мне некого спросить (one negative), never *некого не спросить.
The logical subject stands in the DATIVE and the verb is an INFINITIVE; there is no nominative subject: Мне нечего делать, Ему некуда идти. Past / future use было / будет: Мне было нечего делать.
With a preposition, не- splits but keeps the stress, the dative subject, and the infinitive: Мне не с кем поговорить, Ей не о чем беспокоиться.
examples: Мне нечего делать. (I have nothing to do.) Мне = dative, делать = infinitive, no second не.
Ему некого позвать на помощь. (He has no one to call for help.) Ему = dative, позвать = infinitive.
Нам негде остановиться в этом городе. (We have nowhere to stay in this city.) Нам = dative, негде.
Ей некогда отдыхать. (She has no time to rest.) Ей = dative, некогда + infinitive.
Мне не с кем посоветоваться. (I have no one to consult with.) preposition split, dative + infinitive.
Тебе было нечего бояться. (You had nothing to be afraid of.) past with было, neuter impersonal.

tables.title: The не- family by question word

items.promptEnglish: I have absolutely nothing to do this evening.
items.hint: Subject is in the dative (Мне), the verb is an infinitive (делать), and there is no second не. Which form fits?
items.explanation: The frame is dative subject (Мне) + infinitive (делать) with no second не, which is the не- construction: нечего (stress on не-). It means 'there is nothing for me to do.' Ничего would need a finite verb and a second не (Я ничего не делаю = I am not doing anything), a different structure. Что-то means 'something' and reverses the meaning. Ничего не is the negative pattern, which needs a finite verb, not an infinitive.

items.prompt: Ему _____ спросить дорогу, он здесь никого не знает.
items.promptEnglish: He has no one to ask for directions, he knows nobody here.
items.hint: Dative subject (Ему) + infinitive (спросить), no second не. Spell and stress the prefix accordingly.
items.explanation: Dative subject Ему + infinitive спросить with no second не gives the не- construction: некого (stress нЕкого), 'he has no one to ask.' Note the contrast in the same sentence: никого не знает is the lesson-4 negative (nominative subject он, finite verb, second не). Кого-то means 'someone' and reverses the sense. Некому is the dative form, but спросить takes a direct object, so the accusative некого is right.

items.promptEnglish: We have nowhere to spend the night, all the hotels are full.
items.hint: Dative subject (Нам) + infinitive (переночевать) about a LOCATION. No second не.
items.explanation: A location with a dative subject (Нам) and an infinitive (переночевать) and no second не is негде: 'we have nowhere to spend the night.' Нигде belongs to the lesson-4 negatives and needs a second не (нигде не нашли). Где-то means 'somewhere' and reverses the meaning. Негде не is not a real form; the construction never adds a second не.

items.prompt: Ей _____ заниматься хобби, она всё время работает.
items.promptEnglish: She has no time to pursue hobbies, she works all the time.
items.hint: Dative subject (Ей) + infinitive (заниматься). The meaning is 'no time,' not 'never.'
items.explanation: With a dative subject and an infinitive, некогда means 'there is no time to': Ей некогда заниматься хобби. Никогда means 'never' and needs a finite verb plus a second не (она никогда не отдыхает). Когда-то means 'at some point / once.' Никогда не is the negative pattern, which needs a finite verb, not an infinitive.

items.prompt: В прошлом году нам _____ было ехать в отпуск, не было денег.
items.promptEnglish: Last year we had nowhere to go on vacation, we had no money.
items.hint: Direction ('to go'), dative subject (нам), past with было. No second не.
items.explanation: Direction with a dative subject and infinitive (ехать) takes некуда; the past is formed with neuter было: нам некуда было ехать. Никуда is the lesson-4 negative and needs a second не (мы никуда не ездили = we went nowhere). Куда-то means 'somewhere' and reverses the sense. Никуда не needs a finite verb, not an infinitive.

items.promptEnglish: I have no one to talk to about what's been bothering me.
items.hint: Dative subject (Мне) + infinitive (поговорить), preposition с. The не- splits and keeps its stress.
items.explanation: The не- construction with a preposition splits like the negatives but keeps the dative subject, the infinitive, and the stressed не-: Мне не с кем поговорить ('I have no one to talk with'). Ни с кем is the lesson-4 negative and would need a finite verb plus a second не (Я ни с кем не говорю). С кем-то means 'with someone' and reverses the meaning. Никем не needs a finite verb, not an infinitive.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have nobody to tell this news to.
errorCorrection.explanation: This is the impersonal 'nobody to do X' construction: dative subject + не-form + infinitive, with the stress on не-: некому рассказать. Никому belongs to the other system, the ни- negation that requires не on a finite verb (я никому не рассказал).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This evening I have nothing to occupy myself with.
errorCorrection.explanation: The verb заняться governs the instrumental (заняться чем-то), so the не- pronoun must take the instrumental form: нечем заняться. Нечего is the genitive/accusative, correct with verbs like делать (нечего делать) but not with заняться. Ничем is the double-negation pronoun that needs a finite negated verb (я ничем не занят), not an infinitive. Нечему is the dative. The pronoun declines to match what the infinitive requires, here the instrumental нечем.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мне не к кого обратиться за советом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have nobody to turn to for advice.
errorCorrection.explanation: Обратиться takes к + dative (обратиться к кому-то), so inside the split не- construction the pronoun must be the dative кому: не к кому. Не к кого uses the genitive/accusative кого, which к never governs. Ни к кому is the double-negation pronoun, which would need a finite negated verb (я ни к кому не обратился), not an infinitive. Некому is the non-split form, but once a preposition enters, the не- pronoun splits into three written words around it: не к кому.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ не боюсь — у меня всё под контролем. (Plain negative: nominative я, finite verb, second не.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I am afraid of nothing - everything is under control.
minimalPairs.explanation: Here the subject is nominative (я), the verb is finite (боюсь), and there is a second не: this is the lesson-4 negative, so ничего (stress ничегО), 'I fear nothing.' Нечего belongs to the dative + infinitive construction (Мне нечего бояться = I have nothing to be afraid of), which has no second не.

minimalPairs.context: Мне _____ бояться: всё уже позади. (Construction: dative мне, infinitive бояться, no second не.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I have nothing to be afraid of: it's all behind me now.
minimalPairs.explanation: The frame is dative subject (Мне) + infinitive (бояться) with no second не, which is the не- construction: нечего (stress нЕчего). It means 'there is nothing for me to fear.' Ничего would require a finite verb and a second не, a different structure.

reviewVocab.definition: 'there is no one / nothing to do X': dative subject + infinitive, no second не, stress on the prefix не-.
reviewVocab.example: Мне нечего делать. Ему некого спросить.

reviewVocab.definition: stress distinguishes the construction (нЕкого, no second не, dative + infinitive) from the plain negative (никогО, second не, nominative + finite verb).
reviewVocab.example: Мне некого спросить (no one to ask) vs Я никого не спросил (I asked nobody).

reviewVocab.term: не с кем / не о чем
reviewVocab.definition: with a preposition the не- splits but keeps the stress, the dative subject, and the infinitive.
reviewVocab.example: Ей не с кем пойти в кино.
